notes: Fun-ASR-Nano-2512 through the zoo sample app asr_litertlm (one app for three LiteRT-LM speech bundles: a model picker, hold-to-talk up to 30 s, three FLEURS clips of 9.72 / 6.42 / 11.04 s) on litertlm-android 0.17.1, the published file of litert-community/Fun-ASR-Nano-2512 (snapshot d3769ad6) pushed with adb (HF cache blob = the sha256 below; md5 on the phone equal to the Mac copy). The device check runs in the instrumentation process (cpuset /foreground in this lane's measurements of the same phone), not the app on screen. latency_p50_ms = the median of the three clips' sendMessage walls (one Conversation per clip, encoder + language model), rtf = their sum / the audio seconds; every clip's text equals the expected text (the Mac CPU answer of litert-lm-api 0.17.1), so output_match stays null (#173(2)); peak_mem_mb = the largest VmHWM the check printed (the instrumentation process, memory-mapped bundle pages included). Frequency-capped reference values (#181(3)): both rows ran with the CPU ceilings at 2.23 / 2.23 GHz. The gpu row puts the language model on the GPU (prefill and decode signatures whole on LITERT_CL, evidence) while the audio encoder stays on the CPU (XNNPACK 4965 of 4975 nodes), as #181(2); it is not faster than the CPU row under the same ceiling. The uncapped CPU rerun of the next day is 0.17.1/2026-10-10/fun-asr-nano-2512__galaxy-s26.json. The 2026-09-27 rows of the same file come from the earlier Kotlin demo app (another harness).
quantization: LM int8 dynamic (int8 embedding table), fp32 activations declared on the prefill/decode section; audio encoder fp16 weights, fp32 compute (30.24 s window)
